pretreatments.description: Concentrated phosphoric acid pretreatment, involving heating the substrate with 83–85.9% phosphoric acid in a water bath at 50°C for 50 minutes, followed by washing with cold acetone, distilled water, and acetone washing to neutralize pH and remove solvents.

Organosolv pretreatment, involving mixing the substrate with 75% v/v ethanol and sulfuric acid (1% w/w) in a stainless steel reactor at 150°C for 30 minutes, followed by separation, neutralization, drying at 40°C, and storage.

Dilute sulfuric acid pretreatment, involving mixing the substrate with 0.5% w/w sulfuric acid in a 500 mL reactor at 140°C for 5 minutes, followed by separation, washing with distilled water, neutralization, and drying at 40°C.

Acid pretreatment (mechanical degradation), involving grinding the substrates into small pieces (<2 cm), drying at room temperature, and screening to achieve powder with particle size between 295 and 833 µm.
Steam pretreatment, involving steaming the spruce wastes at 220°C for a time duration to improve carbohydrate enzymatic hydrolysis yield.
Alkali pretreatment, involving the use of NaOH, thiourea, urea, and polyethylene glycol at −15°C to improve biogas yield from hardwood and spruce.
N-methylmorpholine-N-oxide (NMMO) pretreatment, involving using an industrial solvent at 130°C for 15 hours to improve biogas production from spruce.
